memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow-up of BPH and IBS.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports mild urinary frequency and occasional abdominal bloating, no worsening.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78 mmHg, weight 78 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 27.0 (obese). Abdomen soft, non-tender, no masses. Prostate examination not performed today.
IMPRESSION: BPH stable on current meds. IBS controlled with mebeverine and ispaghula. Advised weight reduction as BMI obese; counselled on reduced carbohydrate intake and daily 30‑minute walk.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg at night, finasteride 5 mg daily, mebeverine 135 mg twice daily, ispaghula husk 5 g daily, loperamide 2 mg as needed. Return if new urinary retention, severe abdominal pain, fever >39°C, or blood in stools. Patient to repeat list.

Reason for visit: review of labs and symptom check.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient says urinary flow improved, occasional bloating after meals.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/80, weight 77 kg, BMI 26.5 (overweight). Abdomen mild tenderness in left lower quadrant, no guarding.
IMPRESSION: BPH responding to meds; PSA normal. IBS mild; consider adding fibre. Advised weight loss as BMI overweight; diet low‑fat, increase activity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Add ispaghula husk 5 g BD if bloating persists. Return if worsening urinary symptoms, severe abdominal pain, fever >39°C, or rectal bleeding.

Reason for visit: annual review and influenza vaccination.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports good urinary control, occasional loose stools after spicy food.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78, weight 76 kg, BMI 26.2 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no tenderness.
IMPRESSION: BPH stable. IBS mild; lipid and glucose within target. Advised weight reduction as BMI overweight; increase vegetables, limit fried foods.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg HS, finasteride 5 mg OD, mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Influenza vaccine given today 2025-10-25. Return if new urinary retention, severe abdominal pain, fever >39°C, or blood in stools.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Ultrasound KUB with post‑void residual: Prostate volume 28 mL, no focal lesion. Post‑void residual 15 mL (normal <50). No hydronephrosis. Impression: Benign prostatic hyperplasia, no obstructive uropathy.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Refer to Dr S. Rao, Urology, for evaluation of persistent lower urinary tract symptoms despite medical therapy. Include PSA, ultrasound results, and medication list.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Urology review: Symptoms mild, prostate size benign. Recommend continuing current meds, consider repeat PSA in 6 months. No surgical intervention needed at present.

memories.author: D03

Reason for visit: post‑referral check and medication review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports no change in urinary symptoms, occasional abdominal discomfort after meals.
EXAMINATION: BP 129/79, weight 75 kg, BMI 25.9 (overweight). Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in suprapubic area.
IMPRESSION: BPH stable per urology advice. IBS symptoms mild; consider trial of loperamide PRN. Advised weight reduction as BMI overweight; reduce portion sizes, walk 30 min daily.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg HS, finasteride 5 mg OD, mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Return if worsening urinary pain, fever >39°C, severe diarrhoea, or blood in stools.

Reason for visit: routine follow-up and symptom assessment.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient says urinary flow good, occasional bloating after lentils.
EXAMINATION: BP 127/77, weight 74 kg, BMI 25.6 (overweight). Abdomen soft, non‑tender.
IMPRESSION: BPH controlled. IBS mild; consider reducing legume intake. Advised weight reduction as BMI overweight; increase fruit, avoid fried snacks.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Add mebeverine 135 mg TDS if bloating persists. Return if new urinary retention, severe abdominal pain, fever >39°C, or rectal bleeding.

memories.text: Via clinic app: 'I have been feeling more urgency to urinate in the mornings and mild lower abdominal cramp after breakfast. Otherwise fine.'

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: address new urinary urgency and abdominal cramp.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports morning urgency and mild cramp after breakfast, no fever or bleeding.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/80, weight 73 kg, BMI 25.2 (overweight). Abdomen mild suprapubic tenderness, no distension.
IMPRESSION: Possible BPH progression with mild irritation; IBS may contribute to cramp. Advised weight reduction as BMI overweight; avoid large meals, increase water intake.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase tamsulosin to 0.4 mg BD, continue finasteride 5 mg OD, mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Return if worsening pain, fever >39°C, haematuria, or inability to pass urine.
